key_insight: This paper shows that unlabelled neural spike data can be used to pretrain decoders that generalize better across sessions, reducing dependence on expensive behavioural labels. The proposed MOJO approach extends spike-based neural decoding beyond purely supervised training.
problem_solved: Existing high-performing spike-based neural decoders rely on supervised learning, which requires paired behavioural labels and limits training to labelled datasets. This makes it hard to scale decoding models across many neural recordings and experimental sessions.
method: Introduce MOJO, a masked autoencoder-style pretraining framework for neural spike data.
Train on unlabelled neural activity to learn generalizable representations before fine-tuning for decoding tasks.
Leverage spike-level tokenization so the model can benefit from multi-session pretraining and improve robustness across datasets.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners in neuroscience, this provides a practical path to build stronger decoders using abundant unlabelled data instead of relying only on scarce labelled recordings. It could improve brain-computer interfaces, closed-loop control systems, and other neural technologies that need reliable cross-session decoding.

paper_title: Leveraging unlabelled data for generalizable neural population decoding
